lean.statement:
(μ : Measure E) [IsFiniteMeasure μ]
    (D : Lp ℝ 2 μ →ₗ.[ℝ] Lp E 2 μ) (hD : D.IsClosable)
    (hgraph : ∀ (a : Lp ℝ 2 μ) (H : Lp E 2 μ), (a,H) ∈ D.graph ↔
      ∃ φ : E → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ ∞ φ ∧ HasCompactSupport φ ∧
        a =ᵐ[μ] φ ∧ H =ᵐ[μ] gradient φ)
    {f : E → ℝ} (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f) (hc : HasCompactSupport f) :
    ∃ hp : MemLp f 2 μ, ∃ hq : MemLp (gradient f) 2 μ,
      (hp.toLp f,hq.toLp (gradient f)) ∈ D.closure.graph
approved_definition_context: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable space and canonical Lebesgue volume, including dimension zero. All section ambient instances remain part of the contract. NNReal denotes nonnegative real scalars.

Lp F 2 mu is the actual L2 quotient space; MemLp means a measurable representative with finite L2 norm. MemLp.toLp embeds the actual function class and agrees mu-a.e. Inner products of L2 classes integrate pointwise real inner products against mu.

ContDiff R 1 means C1; infinity means smooth. gradient f is the Riesz representative of the actual Frechet derivative fderiv R f. HasCompactSupport means the topological closure of nonzero support is compact.

LinearPMap is a real-linear partial operator on its stated submodule domain. Its graph consists of pairs of a domain element and its actual output. D.IsClosable means its topological graph closure is single-valued; D.closure is that same closed operator. Coercions from its domain and from L2 classes choose the usual representatives. No test membership is built into these definitions.

Measure.tilted f is exp(f)/integral exp(f) times the original measure. Probability/nonzero normalization is not built into this definition. Kernel is a measurable probability-transition family when IsMarkovKernel holds. A conditional kernel disintegrates the specified joint measure; measure.map is actual pushforward and prod is the actual independent product. stdGaussian denotes the standard real Hilbert Gaussian. All volume or law integrals specify their actual measure.
